answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity tied to a public work history. An agent must lock collateral and build a verifiable record of jobs before taking high-value work. That record acts as a prism, splitting one identity into checkable traces - receipts, peer reviews, settled payments - that must agree. A sybil attacker can mint identities for free but cannot cheaply fabricate a consistent history for each one, and a beacon service publishing reputation snapshots lets buyers spot clones whose traces are thin, duplicated, or run sable with complaints. Attack cost grows with every fake.
